correctness.rationale: The defining equations and rank bounds are invariant under diagonal change of basis. A generic one-parameter subgroup separates all matrix-coordinate weights, so fixed points are pairs of matrix units. For X=E_{ji} and Y=E_{lk}, the two compositions vanish exactly when l!=i and k!=j, producing a(a-1)b(b-1) coordinate pairs. Each has rank one in both factors and therefore lies in every rank closure with 1<=c<=a-1. Euler localization is valid for projective complex algebraic varieties without smoothness or irreducibility assumptions. The packaged checker independently enumerates all matrix-unit pairs on a finite grid and rechecks the rank-bound invariance.

originality.rationale: The archival sources study the affine circular-complex variety, its orbit/component structure, affine-Schubert realization, normality, Cohen--Macaulayness, and rational singularities. The inspected full text contains no Euler, Poincare, Betti, topology, or fixed-point calculation. Targeted semantic-database and web searches using the exact equations, biprojective formulation, topology aliases, and matrix-unit fixed-point formulation found no covering statement. The closest own result is for a linear multiprojective chain complex; closing the chain adds the second composition constraint and removes both free endpoints, and does not imply rank-independence across the distinct circular-complex components.
residual_risks: The localization argument is short and may have appeared as folklore or under quiver-moduli terminology.
Older work on projective quotients of radical-square-zero cyclic-quiver representation varieties may contain an equivalent formula.
A stronger motivic or equivariant computation of circular-complex orbit closures could specialize to the same Euler characteristic.

value.rationale: Circular-complex components are classical algebraic varieties with a substantial literature on their singularities and affine-Schubert geometry. The theorem gives a clean global topological invariant after the natural separate projectivization of the two nonzero arrows. Its rank-independence is structurally informative: all nontrivial component closures, despite different dense ranks and geometry, have the same Euler characteristic. The formula also has a transparent ambient ratio (1-1/a)(1-1/b) and detects the sharp emptiness boundary a=1. This is a natural family-level invariant of the archival object rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
